scenes.caption: Right, acute, obtuse — spot the size
scenes.narration: Angles get their names from their size. A right angle is exactly 90 degrees. Smaller than that is acute, bigger is obtuse.

shape.text: Name the angle: right, acute, obtuse

steps.text: Under 90° is acute, over 90° is obtuse

scenes.caption: Measuring with a protractor
scenes.narration: Line the protractor centre dot up with the vertex, and the baseline with one arm. Then read where the other arm crosses the scale.

shape.text: Put the centre dot on the vertex, the baseline on one arm.
read where the other arm crosses the scale

steps.text: Centre on the vertex, baseline on one arm

scenes.caption: Angles on a straight line, angles at a point
scenes.narration: Two angles sharing a straight line always add to 180 degrees. And a full spin around one point is 360 degrees.

shape.text: two angles on a straight line always make 180°
spin once all the way round: 360 degrees

steps.text: 180° on a line, 360° all the way round

scenes.caption: Triangle angle sum, quadrilateral corners
scenes.narration: Add the three corners of any triangle and you always get 180 degrees. A rectangle has four right angles, so 360. And in a parallelogram, opposite angles match.

shape.text: a rectangle has four right angles — 360° in all

scenes.caption: Misconception: longer arms, same angle
scenes.narration: It is a trap: the long arms look bigger, but the angle only measures the turn between the arms. Same turn, same angle.

shape.text: Watch out: longer arms ≠ bigger angle
same angle — the arm length changes nothing

steps.text: Only the turn between the arms matters
